$provenance: Vendored from https://github.com/JoyChou93/java-sec-code (2.6k-star vulnerable-by-design Java/Spring Boot security demo, no upstream LICENSE file — used here strictly as a small unmodified source excerpt for internal security-QA testing, matching how the existing corpus vendors intentionally-vulnerable teaching code) at pinned commit 4711f4e186258c6e0dd5c3863e7c9592e7e9026a (2024-06-28). Trimmed to 4 of its ~30 one-vulnerability-class-per-file controllers (SQLI, SSRF, XXE, CommandInject) + pom.xml + application.properties — the other controllers (Fastjson, Shiro, SpEL, JWT, XStream, etc.) and supporting DAO/mapper/service classes were dropped as out of scope. Every finding below was hand-verified by reading this exact vendored source (see corpus/README.md for the sampling method). Do not "fix" these — they are the labels the precision/recall gate scores against.

expectedFindings.description: jdbc_sqli_vul string-concatenates the untrusted `username` request parameter into a raw SQL string and runs it via `Statement.executeQuery()` (classic JDBC SQL injection).

jdbc_ps_vuln (the file's own doc comment: 'Incorrect use of prepareStatement') string-concatenates the untrusted `username` request parameter into the SQL text BEFORE handing it to `PreparedStatement` — the `?` placeholder is never used, so parameterization buys nothing (classic JDBC SQL injection, same class as `gt_javaseccode_sqli` but a distinct method/line). A real pipeline scan surfaced this as an apparent false positive; re-reading confirmed it is a genuine, independently-exploitable vulnerability the initial hand-verification pass simply hadn't catalogued (same precedent as PyGoat's `mitre_lab_17_api`/`views.py:560` additions — corpus/README.md's sampling method, point 4).

URLConnectionVuln passes the untrusted `url` request parameter straight to a `URLConnection` helper with no scheme/host allowlist (SSRF; the sibling `/urlConnection/sec` endpoint shows the secured version with an `isHttp` + SSRF-hook check).
xmlReaderVuln parses the raw, unauthenticated request body with a default `XMLReaderFactory`-created `XMLReader` — external entity resolution is not disabled, so a crafted DOCTYPE achieves XXE.
codeInject concatenates the untrusted `filepath` request parameter into a `sh -c` command line run via `ProcessBuilder` (OS command injection).

codeInjectHost (the file's own doc comment: 'Host Injection', with a working `Host: hacked by joychou;cat /etc/passwd` payload example) concatenates the untrusted `Host` request header into a `sh -c curl <host>` command line run via `ProcessBuilder` — same class as `gt_javaseccode_cmdi` but a distinct method/sink/taint-source (header, not a query parameter). A real pipeline scan surfaced this as an apparent false positive; re-reading confirmed it is a genuine, independently-exploitable vulnerability the initial hand-verification pass simply hadn't catalogued (same precedent as PyGoat's additions — corpus/README.md's sampling method, point 4).
Hard-coded `spring.datasource.password` (a literal MySQL password, not an `${ENV}` reference) committed to source control; rotation requires a human.
